step: power-on to playing (resume landing)
what_happened: TV was awake in the client, paused inside Archer S08E05 at 10:57/20:20 with the transport overlay up and focus on Play. Server PlaybackProgress for episode 781 shows position 657/1220 updated 08:02:01, so the paused session was still beaconing correctly.
expected: power-on lands either playing or on a resume affordance that needs one press
verdict: already frictionless for the resume case (1 press). Not a defect. Keep as the reference point for M1/M2.
evidence: adb screencap 2026-11-19T08:01 /tmp/tv-now.png; sqlite3 -readonly PlaybackProgress mediaId=781

step: power-on -> Home -> Continue Watching -> Play (press count)
what_happened: Not measured: the device is mid-session (paused inside an episode, beacons live). Pressing Back would stop playback and discard the owner's place, so the walk was deferred rather than hijacking the remote.
expected: measured when the TV is at idle (screen off or launcher) so the walk disturbs nothing
verdict: BLOCKED by device-in-use guard; first measurement of M1/M2 still owed.
evidence: adb dumpsys: mCurrentFocus=com.mediarr.mediarr_client/.MainActivity, mWakefulness=Awake

step: Home -> the next episode after leaving playback
what_happened: Back from a paused player lands on Home in 1 press — good. But the Continue Watching list is fetched once at app start and never refreshed: the TV offered 'Archer (2009) S08E04 46%' while the server's /api/playback/continue-watching returned S08E05 at 53.9% first, and the DB row for S08E05 had just been updated (657/1220 s). Every episode watched after launch leaves Home one episode behind, so the owner has to go Series -> season -> episode to find the real next thing.
expected: Home offers the episode that was just left, at its saved position, with no navigation detour
verdict: DEFECT — client caches continueWatchingProvider for the app lifetime.
evidence: screenshots /tmp/tv2.png (paused S08E05) and /tmp/home-back.png (Home offers S08E04 46%); server continue-watching returned mediaId 781 S8E5 53.9%; DB PlaybackProgress 781 position 657 updated 15:44:21

step: TV-off semantics: does the display ever sleep?
what_happened: The client had been paused on one frame since 08:01 (identical screenshot sha256 at 15:36). Wake Locks size=0, so no app or player holds the device awake; the display stays on because the device setting mScreenOffTimeoutSetting=2147483646 (effectively never) — a device/developer-option setting on the Shield, not Mediarr holding a lock.
expected: the display sleeps on its own idle timeout, or the app returns to Home after a long pause
verdict: NOT an app defect (device setting). Flagged for the owner: whether the TV should be allowed to sleep is their call; also a candidate UX improvement (auto-exit a paused player after N minutes) if the setting stays as is.
evidence: dumpsys power: Wake Locks: size=0, mScreenOffTimeoutSetting=2147483646, mHoldingDisplaySuspendBlocker=true; screenshot sha256 3d0d483b… identical at 08:01 and 15:36

step: leave playback and return to Home with fresh state
what_happened: FIXED and verified on the TV (build 120 / 1.3.96). Before: Back from the player landed on Home with the previous episode (S08E04 46%) even though the server returned S08E05 53.9%; Continue Watching was fetched once at app start and never refreshed. After: exit -> Home shows hero 'Archer (2009) S08E06' and first tile 'Archer (2009) S08E06 58%' — the episode that had just been playing. Also refreshed on app resume so power-on shows current rows.
expected: Home reflects the session that just ended, with no navigation detour
verdict: FIXED (client), verified on device with before/after screenshots.
evidence: /tmp/fresh-home.png (S08E05 54% before playback), /tmp/home-final.png (S08E06 58% after exit); DB PlaybackProgress 782 position 700 pct 57.8 updated 16:05:39; commit in this round

step: exit playback (the only way out)
what_happened: Back is consumed Kodi-style and only toggles the HUD (deliberate, owner report 2026-11-08), so leaving playback needs the unlabeled Stop button: Back -> Up -> Right -> Right -> Select, 5 presses, while the HUD auto-hides after ~4 s and focus lands on an unexpected control if you are slow. Trying it at adb speed skipped to the next episode and seeked (S08E05 -> S08E06, position 740 -> 1127) instead of exiting. KEYCODE_MEDIA_STOP exits cleanly in one key.
expected: one obvious press leaves playback and saves the position, without hunting an unlabeled corner button
verdict: OPEN — candidate fix: keep Back as HUD-toggle (owner asked) but pause the auto-hide timer while focus is inside the HUD, and give Stop a text label plus a direct key path so exit is deterministic.
evidence: screenshots /tmp/exit1..exit4.png and /tmp/playing1.png; DB position jumps 740 -> 1127; media-stop (keyevent 86) exits in one press

step: folder-import pass, every 30 minutes
what_happened: Each pass reports 'imported N' (3–5) with no new files appearing in the library, and this pass also logged '[BulkImport] Failed to import /data/TV/Archer (2009)': fetch failed' and the same for Mr. Inbetween (metadata fetch over the VPN). The pass re-attempts folding folders that are already library series, so it burns a 2-minute window per pass and could duplicate a series when the metadata fetch does succeed.
expected: a pass over an unchanged library imports nothing and reports nothing
verdict: OPEN (server). Two sub-defects to separate next cycle: (a) counters report 'imported' for files already in place, (b) library folders are re-attempted as fresh imports instead of being recognised as known series.
evidence: journal 16:01:29, 16:02:21, 16:03:27 ('Folder import: scanned 603, skipped 602, imported 3, failed 2'); no new files under /data/TV or /data/Movies since 07:37; Series count unchanged at 43

step: post-import scan after a paused session (verification of the gate)
what_happened: The 16:31 pass still logged 'a playback session is actively progressing' while the client had the position frozen at 791 s since 16:09. Cause: the gate is conservative for a session it has never seen, and the row it had snapshotted at 16:03 was a different episode (781 -> 782 when a stray key skipped). So the position-based gate converges only on the following pass.
expected: a paused session is not treated as live within one pass
verdict: Gate is correct but conservative by one pass; the root cause is the client beaconing while paused. Client fix (report only while playing; write once on pause/seek/stop) built into APK 121 next.
evidence: journal 16:31:09 deferred + DB PlaybackProgress 782 position 791 frozen since 16:09; gate snapshot mismatch 781 -> 782

step: what 'imported 5' actually does
what_happened: The 16:31 pass reported 'imported 5, failed 0' with no BulkImport failures (network recovered) — and yet no new media file appeared anywhere under /data, nor any new MediaFileVariant row. So the import counter reports success for work that produces nothing, which is why every pass looks busy while the library is unchanged.
expected: an import that reports success creates a variant or moves a file; otherwise it is a skip
verdict: OPEN (server): imported/failed counters over-report. Extras pruning (committed c285ffb4) should remove the featurette retries; the counter lie needs its own fix once the extras change is deployed and observed.
evidence: journal 16:31:09 'imported 5, failed 0'; sqlite3 MediaFileVariant createdAt within the last hour: 0 rows; find /data/TV -newermt 16:20: no files

step: post-import scan while a session is paused (end-to-end proof)
what_happened: With the beacon fix installed (APK 121) and a session paused since 16:40:57 (position 797, no beacon writes for 21+ minutes), the 17:01 folder-import pass logged 'Post-import scan: 0 movie(s), 82 episode(s), 3842 subtitle file(s) detected (247140 ms)' at 17:04:59 instead of the deferred line that every pass produced from 13:01 to 16:31. The extras pruning also removed the two recurring '[BulkImport] Failed to import' errors for Archer and Mr. Inbetween.
expected: a paused session never blocks registration of freshly imported media
verdict: FIXED and verified end-to-end on the live engine (server 37c39d7b + c285ffb4, client 6dba74e5 / APK 121).
evidence: journal 17:00:51 import pass, 17:04:59 post-import scan with 82 episodes and 3,842 subtitle files; DB PlaybackProgress 782 position 797 updated 16:40:57 (frozen, no beacons)

step: CORRECTION to the exit-playback entry (16:07)
what_happened: The earlier entry said the HUD 'auto-hides while the user is walking its controls'. That is wrong: playback_screen._handleKey calls service.showOverlay() for every key while the HUD is visible, which restarts the 4 s window. Re-reading the evidence: each adb screencap takes ~2-3 s, so the HUD hid because I paused to capture between presses, not because input failed to reset the timer.
expected: the ledger states what was actually measured
verdict: CORRECTION. The real defect is the 4-second window itself (see next entry), and the design escalation must use the corrected fact so K3.1 is not asked to fix a non-bug.
evidence: playback_screen.dart ~line 746-750: 'any other key wakes the overlay and restarts the 4 s hide window' -> service.showOverlay() -> _startOverlayTimer()

step: exit playback: why presses turn into seeks
what_happened: While the HUD is hidden, Left/Right are seek keys (a deliberate design: seek without waking the HUD). The HUD hides 4 s after the last input. An exit walk is 5 presses plus human hesitation, so pressing Right just after the window lapsed seeks instead of moving focus: in one measured attempt the position jumped 740 s -> 1127 s and the episode changed. So the same key means 'move focus' or 'seek 10 s' depending on a timer the viewer cannot see.
expected: arrows always mean one thing while the viewer is in control of the HUD, and the exit cost is the same every time
verdict: OPEN, design decision pending K3.1 (provider down, three failed attempts). Candidate directions: longer idle window, a persistent visible hint that arrows seek while hidden, and a one-press exit affordance.
evidence: screenshots /tmp/exit1.png (overlay visible, Back focused), /tmp/exit3.png (overlay hidden after ~4 s), DB position 740 -> 1127 and episode 781 -> 782

step: the 5-press exit walk, measured cleanly (all keys within one second)
what_happened: From playing Archer S08E06, the documented exit walk Back -> Up -> Right -> Right -> Select was sent as one fast key sequence (so the 4 s HUD window could not lapse between presses). Result: instead of leaving playback the client opened the NEXT episode, Archer S08E07 'Gramercy, Halberd!', and resumed it at its stored position 805 s. So the focus path from the top bar reaches the skip-next control, and Select on it starts different content than the viewer was watching.
expected: the same 5 presses leave playback and save the place, every time
verdict: OPEN — P1 class: an attempt to exit can switch episodes (wrong content, stale position) with no confirmation. Precise focus graph must come from the K3.1 spec; candidate constraint regardless of design: Select must never start different content while the viewer is trying to leave.
evidence: screenshot /tmp/exitwalk.png (S08E07 at 13:19); DB PlaybackProgress 783 position 805 updated 17:27:41; sequence sent via one adb 'input keyevent 4 19 22 22 23'

step: TV standby -> power on -> intended thing playing
what_happened: Put the TV to sleep with the power key and woke it: the client came back on the connection screen — 'No servers found. Try manual entry.' — with the system IME already open and a stale 192.168.1.100 in the host field, while the server was up at 192.168.10.65 (health ok). A relaunch connected immediately, so the failure is the boot-time discovery racing the network coming back, not a real absence of servers. The screen had no retry: one failed probe became a typing job with a TV remote.
expected: power-on lands on Home (or connects within a few seconds) with zero typing
verdict: DEFECT, fixed this cycle: the screen now retries discovery every 4 s (15 fast, then every 15 s), retries on app resume, and no longer autofocuses the host field, so the IME cannot appear unasked. Root cause of the retry not working at first: two concurrent stopScan() calls awaited the same subscription cancel and never completed — fixed in DiscoveryService.stopScan.
evidence: screenshot /tmp/sleepstate.png (connect screen + IME, 192.168.1.100); hostname -I = 192.168.10.65, /api/health ok; relaunch screenshot /tmp/relaunch.png shows Home connected

step: files on disk -> visible on Home (the gap between 'downloaded' and 'playable')
what_happened: Fifteen video files sat in the library invisible to the client because folder-import skipped any folder whose name matched a library title: the Sinners (2025) duplicate, Ballerina (2025), Beetlejuice (1988), The Running Man (2025), The Accountant², an SNL special, an X-Men documentary and others. The 18:01 pass now reports 'scanned 603 folder(s), skipped 590, imported 14 item(s), failed 0' and registered 14 variants at 18:00:10-13; Movie rows went 574 -> 576. Verified on the TV: Home 'Recently Added' now leads with The Running Man, its detail page shows poster/year/size with Play focused, and playing it wrote playback progress (movie 576).
expected: a file the operator files into /data becomes playable without any extra step
verdict: FIXED (server, 72cfab11) and verified on the engine and the device. The honest '无字幕' badge on that movie is accurate: it has no subtitles yet, which is the next Journey-1 gap for newly acquired films.
evidence: journal 18:00:52 import line; MediaFileVariant createdAt 18:00:10-13 (X-Men The Mutant Watch, Walls Have Ears, The Running Man 2025, The Tattooist's Son, The Accountant², ...); Movie count 576; screenshots /tmp/newcontent.png and /tmp/runningman.png; PlaybackProgress MOVIE 576 position 4 at 18:06:58

step: new movie gets 中英 subtitles and the client shows them
what_happened: The Running Man (2025) was registered this round but showed 无字幕. Acquired an official Simplified pack from zimuku (detail 223550, 2,799 cues, 官方 iTunes WEB translation), verified it against the release (96.9% cue overlap with the existing YTS English sidecar, drift <1 s at 600/1800/3600/7200 s), built the house-style bilingual sidecar (Chinese line, English under, 2,247/2,799 cues paired) and placed it next to the video. subtitle-sync then aligned it (kept the original as .orig).
expected: the client shows the available subtitle languages without any extra step
verdict: DONE and verified on the TV: the movie's detail page now shows the 中文 badge where it showed 无字幕 an hour earlier; DB VariantSubtitleTrack has en + zho EXTERNAL rows; receipt in /config/subtitle-acquire-receipts.jsonl.
evidence: receipt jsonl entry 2026-11-19T18:20; DB tracks 17719 (en) + 17722 (zho) for variant 15808; screenshot /tmp/rm-badge.png

step: how long a placed sidecar takes to appear (defect found while verifying)
what_happened: Only the heavy nightly library scan (02:00, 247 s measured) registered external sidecars, so a sidecar placed by the operator or a subtitle cycle stayed invisible until the next night. Fixed with a bounded 'subtitle-sidecar-register' pass every 10 minutes (40 variants, rotating cursor). First live pass at 18:30:06 logged '2 track(s) registered (40 variant(s) checked)' and the 中文 badge appeared.
expected: a sidecar on disk becomes a selectable track within minutes, not hours
verdict: FIXED (3a98be0a) and verified live at 18:30:06. 4/4 sidecar tests.
evidence: journal 18:30:06 'Sidecar subtitles: 2 track(s) registered (40 variant(s) checked)'; plan 8.7

step: sidecar registration must not register its own working files
what_happened: The new pass registered ffsubsync's temporary `<sidecar>.sync.srt` as a second Chinese track; ffsubsync renames that file over the sidecar when it finishes, so the row dangled and the client would have offered a subtitle that cannot load. Fixed twice: working files (.sync/.orig/.bak) are excluded, and external tracks whose file is gone are pruned when the video itself is present (never when the mount is missing). The 18:40 pass logged '0 track(s) registered, 1 dangling track(s) pruned' and the movie now has exactly en + zho.
expected: the track list only ever contains files that can be loaded
verdict: FIXED (0eec66cf + a895bb61) and verified live at 18:40:10. 6/6 sidecar tests.
evidence: journal 18:40:10; DB VariantSubtitleTrack for variant 15808 now 2 rows (en, zho)

step: the recurring 'imported 3 item(s)' churn: what it actually was
what_happened: The unregistered-file list shrank to exactly three: two 'American Dad S16E21/E22' files and Mr. Inbetween 'S00E01'. The American Dad pair are the same episodes the library already has as S17E02 'Downtown' and S17E03 'Cheek to Cheek' (ffprobe durations 1269.397 vs 1269.439/1269.503, same titles) - the release numbered the season differently. The Mr. Inbetween file is the 2005 film the series is based on, parsing as S00E01 while the series has no season-0 row, so the import could never link it.
expected: an unchanged library imports nothing and says nothing
verdict: Both halves handled. The two duplicate copies were moved to /data/_quarantine/duplicates-20261119-late/ (390 MB) with a manifest that names the kept file and how the match was verified; nothing deleted. Importer fix: files whose SxxEyy has no episode row are reported as 'files with no episode row' instead of being re-imported.
evidence: quarantine manifest.jsonl; first honest pass at 19:00:31: 'imported 0 item(s), failed 0, ... 1 file(s) with no episode row: Mr. Inbetween - S00E01 - The Magician (2005).mp4'

step: log noise: folders reported as unmatched while holding known files
what_happened: Every pass also reported 'unmatched Archer (2009) Season 8'. That folder is where the library actually linked S08 (episodes 8x1-8x8 point into it); the folder name is just unknown to the title registry, so the importer tried a metadata search it could never use.
expected: folders with nothing to import are skipped without a metadata lookup
verdict: FIXED (f5ebf2ae): any folder whose video files are all registered is skipped before matching. 16/16 folder-import tests; verification on the 19:30 pass.
evidence: DB Episode rows 8x1-8x8 under /data/TV/Archer (2009) Season 8/Season 8/; journal 19:00:31 unmatched line
